info.name: Grav CMS API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Grav CMS RESTful API plugin.

## Setup

1. Set the `base_url` variable to your Grav site URL (e.g., `https://localhost/grav-api`)
2. Set the `api_key` variable to a valid API key (generate via `bin/plugin api keys:generate`)
3. Set `grav_environment` to your Grav environment (default: `localhost`)
4. All requests include `X-API-Key` and `X-Grav-Environment` headers automatically

## Authentication

All requests (except `/auth/*` endpoints) require the `X-API-Key` header.
The `X-Grav-Environment` header is included on all requests to ensure correct environment context.

Where a page sits among its siblings, for page-to-page navigation:

zero-based position and the number of siblings.

`GET /pages?children_of=<parent>&sort=default&order=asc` lists them
(`children_of=/` for a top-level page), and `first_child` is the first
row of the same listing for the page's own children. Every row is
serialized exactly like a `GET /pages?fields=summary` row, including

never the whole site.

`next` for the last and `first_child` when the page has no children.
A page that its parent's listing leaves out (a folder with no content
file) gets `index: -1` and null `prev` and `next`.

Requires `api.pages.read`, and the page's own rules must allow

item.name: Upload a file for a blueprint file field

exec: // Generated from openapi.yaml by tests/newman/sync-collection.php; the Newman suite skips it.

request.description:
Destination-aware upload for blueprint `type: file` fields (a theme logo, a plugin asset, an avatar), mirroring classic admin's `taskFilesUpload`. Requires `api.media.write`.
The target folder comes from the field's `destination`: a Grav stream (`theme://images`, `user://media`), a `self@:subpath` token resolved against `scope`, or a plain path relative to `user/`. Absolute paths and `..` segments are rejected.
Every multipart file part is saved (nested file arrays are flattened). Each file is capped at 64 MB, and the field's own `filesize` can only tighten that. Extensions listed in `security.uploads_dangerous_extensions` are refused in any dot-separated part of the name (so `shell.php.jpg` fails), as are config-type extensions (`yaml`, `yml`, `json`, `twig`, `env`, `neon`, `lock`), page content (`md`, `markdown`) and stylesheets (`css`, `scss`, `sass`, `less`). Uploads into `user/accounts/` are restricted to image extensions, and uploads resolving into `user/config/` or `user/env/*/config/` are refused with 403. SVG files are sanitized after saving.
A developer can allow page content or stylesheets for one field by listing them in that field's blueprint, for example `allow_extensions: [css]`. The server reads this from the blueprint that owns `scope` (a plugin or theme config blueprint, the page template's blueprint, or the account blueprint), never from the request: the request only names the field in `field`, and the upload's `destination` must be that field's own `destination`. `allow_extensions` can only lift `md`, `markdown`, `css`, `scss`, `sass` and `less`; dangerous and config-type extensions, the accounts image-only rule and the config directory block always apply.
`self@:` against a `users/<username>` scope for another account needs `api.users.write` or super-admin.

formdata.description: File to upload. Any field name works, and several file parts may be sent in one request.
Owner of the blueprint, used to resolve `self@:` destinations. One of `plugins/<slug>`, `themes/<slug>`, `pages/<route>`, `users/<username>`.

Full name of the blueprint field the upload belongs to, as the form knows it (`custom_css`, `header.stylesheet`). Used together with `scope` to look up the field's `allow_extensions` in the blueprint on the server. Without it, or without `scope`, page content and stylesheets are refused.
Replace the file name with a random one (extension kept).
Add a suffix instead of replacing an existing file of the same name.
Comma-separated allowlist of extensions (`.pdf`, `*.jpg`) or MIME patterns (`image/*`). May also be sent as an array.

request.description:
Remove a file previously saved through `POST /blueprint-upload`, plus its `.meta.yaml` sidecar when present. Requires `api.media.write`.
`path` is the logical path the upload returned, relative to the user root (`user/` prefix optional). Absolute input, `..` and null bytes are rejected. Targets in `user/config/` or `user/env/*/config/` are refused with 403. Under `user/accounts/` only image files may be deleted, and without `api.users.write` only the caller's own avatar (403 otherwise). The same extension denylist as the upload applies, so page content (`.md`) and stylesheets can't be deleted here unless `field` and `scope` name a blueprint field that allows them with `allow_extensions` and the file sits in the folder that field's `destination` resolves to.
The call is idempotent: a file that no longer exists returns 204.

request.description:
Read-only file listing for blueprint fields that declare a `folder:` option (filepicker, mediapicker), mirroring classic admin's `taskGetFilesInFolder`. Requires `api.media.read`.
`folder` may be a Grav stream (`user://media`, `theme://images`, `account://`), a `self@:subpath` token resolved against `scope`, or a plain path relative to `user/`. A folder that does not exist yet returns an empty list with `meta.exists: false`.

request.description:
Drops overrides from the active configuration layer so the values fall back to the parent layer (defaults for a base write, defaults plus base for an environment write). Requires `api.config.write`. Writes to `system`, `security` and `plugins/api` also need an API super user, and the tool-managed `scheduler` and `backups` scopes are super-only for reading and writing.
Send `keys` (dotted paths) to remove individual overrides, or `reset: true` to delete the layer's file for that scope entirely. The target layer follows the same rules as `PATCH /config/{scope}`: the `X-Config-Environment` header picks it, an empty value (or `default` / `base`) means the base `user/config`, and when absent the active environment is used if it has a config folder.
The response is the effective configuration after the revert, with secrets masked, and `meta` lists the paths that still override the parent layer. Reverting something the layer does not override (for example `reset: true` when the layer has no file) is still a 200, but `meta.reverted` is false and no `onApiConfigUpdated` event (so no `config.updated` webhook) fires.
